method: Analytic estimates, not a Monte Carlo run. Primary fluence is exp(-mu*x) with mu/rho(2 MeV, water)=0.04942 cm2/g over 10 cm, giving 0.610 per Phi0; inverse-square terms cancel against Phi0 at 110 cm. Scattered fluence (about 0.37 per Phi0) and its spectrum were estimated from typical 2 MeV, 10x10 cm2, 10 cm depth scatter buildup, with the Compton-kinematics shape used for the spectrum. The photon grid ends at 1.4 MeV, so the 2.0 MeV primaries fall outside it and the primary spectrum is zero on the grid. Interaction fractions were computed from mass attenuation coefficients per process. Electron initial spectra used Klein-Nishina Compton electron distributions at 2 MeV and uniform approximations for scattered-photon electrons. Electron fluence was estimated as Kcol divided by the collision stopping power, cross-checked by a slowing-down count. Dose equals collision kerma under CPE. Angular and mean-energy values are rough estimates. Expect roughly 10-20% uncertainty, larger for the spectral and angular quantities.
data_sources: NIST XCOM photon cross sections for water (mu/rho, mu_en/rho); NIST ESTAR collision and radiative stopping powers for water; Klein-Nishina differential cross section for Compton electron spectra and angles; Spencer-Attix water-to-air stopping-power ratio based on ESTAR/ICRU-37 data (approximate, value estimated not computed); PDD estimated from typical 2 MeV 10x10 cm2 depth-dose data.
